declarations.documentation: The live Discord gateway connection (the JS client lives in the sidecar; the handle is opaque).
declarations.name: connection

declarations.checkedType: agent(continuation: agent(value: null) -> T0 with connection | E1, source: env | oauth) -> T0 with throw[api_error | auth_error | missing_secret | server_error] | E1 | io
declarations.documentation:
Provide the Discord gateway connection for the extent of the continuation: resolve @source@ ONCE
(a gateway credential is fixed at connect — the websocket's nature, so a rotation lands on the next
restart, not mid-connection), log in, then serve `connection` to everything downstream. A failed
login (a bad token, a transient network fault) raises `discord_error` (`auth_error` | `api_error`) —
surfacing here rather than on the first send.
declarations.name: provider

parameters.documentation: Where the bot token lives (env key or oauth name); resolved once at connect.
parameters.label: source

parameters.documentation: Runs with `connection` served; its result is the provider's result.
parameters.label: continuation

declarations.documentation:
Connect to Discord and log in; returns an opaque client handle. Raises `discord_error` (`auth_error`
| `api_error`) when the login fails — an invalid token / missing permission is `auth_error`, a transient
network fault `api_error`. Prefer the provider.
declarations.name: create_discord_client

parameters.documentation: The bot token to log in with.
parameters.label: token

token.description: The bot token to log in with.

declarations.signature: external agent create_discord_client(token: string of private) -> string with prelude.throw[discord_error]

declarations.documentation:
Close a Discord connection: destroy the gateway client and drop the handle. The provider arms this
as a `finally`, so the connection dies with the run — a gateway client left alive stays logged in and
keeps receiving events long after its run is gone, a leaked session that still handles messages.
Idempotent: closing an unknown or already-closed handle is a no-op, since a finalizer may run more
than once.
declarations.name: discord_close

parameters.documentation: The opaque client handle `create_discord_client` returned.
parameters.label: client

declarations.documentation:
An authentication / authorization failure: the bot token is invalid or expired (HTTP 401), or the
bot lacks permission in the channel (HTTP 403); @message@ carries Discord's error. The bot cannot
recover on its own — the operator must fix the token or the bot's permissions and restart the run (the
connection is fixed at start). Let it surface so the bot stops loudly rather than silently dropping
every reply.
declarations.name: auth_error

declarations.documentation:
A Discord API call failed for a non-auth reason: a rate limit (HTTP 429), a channel that is not a
sendable text channel, a transient network fault; @message@ carries Discord's error. Usually
per-message or transient, so a bot catches it to drop just that reply and keep serving.
declarations.name: api_error

declarations.documentation:
Low-level: post to a channel on a given client, with any files as attachments, returning the posted
message's id. Raises `auth_error` or `api_error` (`discord_error`) when the Discord API call fails.
Prefer the send_message agent.

declarations.checkedType: agent(channel: string, options: array[string], prompt: string) -> string with connection | throw[api_error | auth_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
Post @prompt@ with one BUTTON per option to a channel and BLOCK until someone there clicks one,
returning the clicked label verbatim — the built-in human-approval UI (an `ai.authorize_monitor`
provider asking an operators' channel, a confirmation step before an irreversible action). Put the
prompt in a channel whose MEMBERSHIP is the trust boundary: any member may click. The wait rides one
external call, so a runtime restart while it is open interrupts it under the at-most-once rule (a
catchable panic) and the posted buttons go stale. That failure is the DESIGNED outcome, not a defect
to absorb here: let the panic ride to your supervisor and restart the asking flow — whoever wanted
the answer asks again — rather than guessing an answer for a click that never landed. Raises
`discord_error` when the post fails.
declarations.name: ask

parameters.documentation: The channel to ask in — its membership is who may answer.
parameters.label: channel

parameters.documentation: The question posted above the buttons.
parameters.label: prompt

parameters.documentation: One button label per option; the clicked label is returned.
parameters.label: options

declarations.documentation:
Post a message to a channel using the ambient Discord client, returning the posted MESSAGE'S ID —
the composable seam a later edit / reaction / thread-reply agent will address a message by, so a
caller that needs to refer back keeps it (and one that does not simply drops it). @files@ attach to
the post. Raises `discord_error` (`auth_error` | `api_error`) when the send fails — catch `api_error`
to keep a bot serving past a transient failure, and let `auth_error` surface so a bad token stops the
bot loudly.
declarations.name: send_message

parameters.label: channel

declarations.checkedType: agent(channel: string, files?: array[file], text: string) -> null with connection | throw[auth_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
Post RESILIENTLY, fire-and-forget — the composition every long-lived bot writes around
`send_message`, packaged: a blank @text@ with no @files@ posts nothing (a quiet protocol's silence);
a transient `api_error` (a rate limit, an unsendable channel) drops just this post so the bot keeps
serving; `auth_error` re-raises so a bad token still stops the bot loudly. The posted message's id
is deliberately dropped — a caller that needs it wants `send_message` and its own error policy.
declarations.name: try_send

declarations.checkedType: agent(channel: string, deliver_to: agent(author: string, channel: string, files: array[file], text: string) -> null with E3) -> never with connection | E3 | io
declarations.documentation:
Serve a channel forever, delivering each incoming message to @deliver_to@ — shaped like
`time.watch` / `google_calendar.watch` so it composes under `parallel [ … ]`. Bot posts (this bot's
own replies included) are not delivered, so replying from @deliver_to@ cannot loop. @author@ is the
sender's raw Discord user id (a snowflake — an opaque numeric id, not a name); hash it
(`crypto.sha256`) before letting it leave the program, e.g. as an AI provider's abuse-attribution
tag.
